q: Mechanisms of breathing are for gas exchange which is the uptake of oxygen from environment and the elimination of ____ from the body.
e: Mechanisms of breathing are for gas exchange which is the uptake of oxygen from environment and the elimination of carbon dioxide from the body. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: The general body surface of most animals lacks sufficient surface area to exchange gases for the whole organism. To solve this limitation is the evolution of respiratory or ____.
e: The general body surface of most animals lacks sufficient surface area to exchange gases for the whole organism. To solve this limitation is the evolution of respiratory or breathing organs. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened.

q: These organs are extensively folded or branched thereby enlarging the available surface area for gas exchange such as gills, tracheae, ____ and other modified structures.
e: These organs are extensively folded or branched thereby enlarging the available surface area for gas exchange such as gills, tracheae, lungs and other modified structures. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: ____ are gas exchange organs for aquatic animals.
e: Gills are gas exchange organs for aquatic animals. Gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: Gills are outfolding of body surfaces that are suspended in ____.
e: Gills are outfolding of body surfaces that are suspended in water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals.

q: Aquatic animals that use gills are polychaetes (marine worms of the phylum Annelida), crustaceans, sea stars and ____.
e: Aquatic animals that use gills are polychaetes (marine worms of the phylum Annelida), crustaceans, sea stars and fish. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces. Many polychaete worms use gills in water.

q: Each gill arch has two rows of gill filaments, composed of flattened plates called ____.
e: Each gill arch has two rows of gill filaments, composed of flattened plates called lamellae. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Blood flowing through capillaries within the lamellae picks up oxygen from the ____.
e: Blood flowing through capillaries within the lamellae picks up oxygen from the water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin.

q: The counter current flow of water and blood causes the continuous diffusion of oxygen from the water into the blood over the entire length of a ____.
e: The counter current flow of water and blood causes the continuous diffusion of oxygen from the water into the blood over the entire length of a capillary. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin. Counter-current flow in fish gills keeps a gradient so more oxygen is extracted.

q: Although the most familiar respiratory structure among terrestrial animals is the lungs, some use tracheae (in insects), book lungs (in spiders and scorpions). Others use ____ (in earthworms, frogs and toads).
e: Although the most familiar respiratory structure among terrestrial animals is the lungs, some use tracheae (in insects), book lungs (in spiders and scorpions). Others use skin (in earthworms, frogs and toads). Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills. Book lungs are stacked gas-exchange plates in some arachnids.

q: Frogs and toads often use the lining of the ____.
e: Frogs and toads often use the lining of the buccal cavity. Buccal cavity is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The lungs are enclosed in the chest or thorax by the rib cage and a muscular sheet of tissue called the ____.
e: The lungs are enclosed in the chest or thorax by the rib cage and a muscular sheet of tissue called the diaphragm. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: Joining each rib to the next are two sets of muscles called ____.
e: Joining each rib to the next are two sets of muscles called intercostal muscles. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: The diaphragm separates the contents of the thorax from the ____.
e: The diaphragm separates the contents of the thorax from the abdomen. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: It is not flat, but a shallow dome shape, with a fibrous middle part forming the 'roof' of the dome, and muscular edges forming the ____.
e: It is not flat, but a shallow dome shape, with a fibrous middle part forming the 'roof' of the dome, and muscular edges forming the walls. Walls is the biological term this statement needs.

q: When breathing in, air enters the nose or mouth and passes down the windpipe or ____.
e: When breathing in, air enters the nose or mouth and passes down the windpipe or trachea. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: The trachea splits into two tubes called the ____, one leading to each lung.
e: The trachea splits into two tubes called the bronchi, one leading to each lung. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Each bronchus divides into smaller and smaller tubes called ____, eventually ending at microscopic air sacs, called alveoli.
e: Each bronchus divides into smaller and smaller tubes called bronchioles, eventually ending at microscopic air sacs, called alveoli. Bronchioles are the finer airways that end in alveoli. Alveoli are tiny lung sacs with a huge surface for diffusion of gases.

q: The walls of trachea and bronchi contain rings of gristle or ____, which support the airway and keep them open when breathing.
e: The walls of trachea and bronchi contain rings of gristle or cartilage, which support the airway and keep them open when breathing. Cartilage keeps airways such as the trachea open. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi.

q: The inside of the thorax is separated from the lungs by two thin, moist membranes called the ____.
e: The inside of the thorax is separated from the lungs by two thin, moist membranes called the pleural membranes. Pleural membranes and fluid let the lungs slide as the thorax changes volume. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: Between the two membranes is a space called the pleural cavity, filled with a thin layer of liquid called ____.
e: Between the two membranes is a space called the pleural cavity, filled with a thin layer of liquid called pleural fluid. Pleural membranes and fluid let the lungs slide as the thorax changes volume. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: ____ means moving air in and out of the lungs.
e: Ventilation means moving air in and out of the lungs. Ventilation is moving air or water across the gas-exchange surface. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: Ventilation depends on the fact that thorax is an ____ cavity.
e: Ventilation depends on the fact that thorax is an airtight cavity. Ventilation is moving air or water across the gas-exchange surface.

q: When breathing, the volume of the thorax change, which alters the pressure inside it. This causes air to move in or out of the ____.
e: When breathing, the volume of the thorax change, which alters the pressure inside it. This causes air to move in or out of the lungs. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: During inhalation, external intercostal muscles ____ and internal intercostal muscles relax.
e: During inhalation, external intercostal muscles contract and internal intercostal muscles relax. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing.

q: During exhalation, external intercostal muscles relax and internal intercostal muscles ____.
e: During exhalation, external intercostal muscles relax and internal intercostal muscles contract. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing.

q: During inhalation, the rib cage causes upward and ____ movement.
e: During inhalation, the rib cage causes upward and outward movement. Outward is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During exhalation, the rib cage causes downward and ____ movement.
e: During exhalation, the rib cage causes downward and inward movement. Inward is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During inhalation, muscles of diaphragm ____.
e: During inhalation, muscles of diaphragm contract. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: During exhalation, muscles of diaphragm ____.
e: During exhalation, muscles of diaphragm relax. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: During inhalation, diaphragm becomes ____.
e: During inhalation, diaphragm becomes flattened. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: During exhalation, diaphragm goes back to its normal ____ shape.
e: During exhalation, diaphragm goes back to its normal dome shape. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: During inhalation, chest ____ in volume.
e: During inhalation, chest increases in volume. Increases is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During exhalation, chest ____ in volume.
e: During exhalation, chest decreases in volume. Decreases is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During inhalation, chest ____ in pressure.
e: During inhalation, chest decreases in pressure. Decreases is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During exhalation, chest ____ in pressure.
e: During exhalation, chest increases in pressure. Increases is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During inhalation, air ____ into the lungs.
e: During inhalation, air enters into the lungs. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: During exhalation, air ____ out of the lungs.
e: During exhalation, air leaves out of the lungs. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: The diffusion of gases takes place from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower ____.
e: The diffusion of gases takes place from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: Cell respiration uses oxygen and produces ____.
e: Cell respiration uses oxygen and produces carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: Plants require oxygen for respiration and carbon dioxide for ____.
e: Plants require oxygen for respiration and carbon dioxide for photosynthesis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: The movement of gases in and out of green plants is via a process called ____.
e: The movement of gases in and out of green plants is via a process called diffusion. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: Single-celled organisms and small and thin organisms rely on ____ for gas exchange.
e: Single-celled organisms and small and thin organisms rely on diffusion for gas exchange. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: In larger organisms, simple diffusion alone is not an efficient way of transporting gases between cells in the body and the gas exchange ____.
e: In larger organisms, simple diffusion alone is not an efficient way of transporting gases between cells in the body and the gas exchange surface. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: The rate of gas exchange is affected by: the area available for diffusion, the distance over which diffusion occurs, the concentration gradient across the gas exchange surface, and the speed with which molecules diffuse through ____.
e: The rate of gas exchange is affected by: the area available for diffusion, the distance over which diffusion occurs, the concentration gradient across the gas exchange surface, and the speed with which molecules diffuse through membranes. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: Efficient gas exchange systems must: have a large surface area to volume ratio, be thin, have mechanisms for maintaining steep concentration gradients across themselves, and be permeable to ____.
e: Efficient gas exchange systems must: have a large surface area to volume ratio, be thin, have mechanisms for maintaining steep concentration gradients across themselves, and be permeable to gases. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened.

q: In daylight, when photosynthesis is going on in green plants, they will be taking in carbon dioxide and giving out ____.
e: In daylight, when photosynthesis is going on in green plants, they will be taking in carbon dioxide and giving out oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: When respiration is going on, they will be taking in oxygen and giving out ____.
e: When respiration is going on, they will be taking in oxygen and giving out carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: In plants, oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse through the stomata and the ____.
e: In plants, oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse through the stomata and the lenticels. Lenticels are cork pores that let woody stems exchange gases. Carbon dioxide enters the leaf through stomata.

q: The stomata are the openings in the epidermis of the plant especially of the ____.
e: The stomata are the openings in the epidermis of the plant especially of the leaves. Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out.

q: A stoma is bounded by a pair of specialized cells known as the ____ which contain the chloroplasts.
e: A stoma is bounded by a pair of specialized cells known as the guard cells which contain the chloroplasts. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: The stomata allow the gas exchange and ____.
e: The stomata allow the gas exchange and transpiration. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: Oxygen produced as a by-product of photosynthesis diffuses out to the atmosphere through these same ____.
e: Oxygen produced as a by-product of photosynthesis diffuses out to the atmosphere through these same openings. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth.

q: The guard cells are responsible for regulating the opening and closing of ____.
e: The guard cells are responsible for regulating the opening and closing of stomata. Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor.

q: Stomatal opening and closing depends on changes in the turgor pressure of the ____.
e: Stomatal opening and closing depends on changes in the turgor pressure of the guard cells. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells.

q: Normally the stomata are opened in the daytime and closed at ____.
e: Normally the stomata are opened in the daytime and closed at night. Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out.

q: In the daytime, when water diffuses into the guard cells by osmosis, their turgor increases and they ____.
e: In the daytime, when water diffuses into the guard cells by osmosis, their turgor increases and they expand. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor. Osmosis is diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane.

q: Due to the relatively inelastic inner wall, the guard cells bend and draw away from each other, so the pore ____.
e: Due to the relatively inelastic inner wall, the guard cells bend and draw away from each other, so the pore opens. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor.

q: If the guard cells lose water, the opposite happens and the pore ____.
e: If the guard cells lose water, the opposite happens and the pore closes. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor.

q: Lenticels are small openings on stems, fruits, tubers and ____.
e: Lenticels are small openings on stems, fruits, tubers and roots. Roots may use air spaces or aerenchyma when soil oxygen is low. Lenticels are cork pores that let woody stems exchange gases.

q: Lenticel provides a pathway for the direct exchange of gases between the internal tissues and atmosphere through it, which is otherwise ____ to gases.
e: Lenticel provides a pathway for the direct exchange of gases between the internal tissues and atmosphere through it, which is otherwise impermeable to gases. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth.

q: Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place between the air and the blood vessels surrounding the ____.
e: Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place between the air and the blood vessels surrounding the alveoli. Alveoli are tiny lung sacs with a huge surface for diffusion of gases. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin.

q: The two lungs contain about seven hundred millions of these tiny air sacs, giving a total surface area of ____.
e: The two lungs contain about seven hundred millions of these tiny air sacs, giving a total surface area of 60m². A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: The blood is separated from the air inside each alveolus by only two cell layers: the cells making up the wall of the alveolus, and the ____ itself.
e: The blood is separated from the air inside each alveolus by only two cell layers: the cells making up the wall of the alveolus, and the capillary wall itself. Each alveolus is a thin-walled sac where oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: This is a distance of less than a thousandth of a millimeter, which provides short diffusion distance for oxygen and ____.
e: This is a distance of less than a thousandth of a millimeter, which provides short diffusion distance for oxygen and carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: In plants, transport of gases is only by simple ____.
e: In plants, transport of gases is only by simple diffusion. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: In humans, deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs via the ____.
e: In humans, deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs via the pulmonary artery. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from heart to lungs. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: The capillaries carrying oxygenated blood from the alveoli join up to form the ____, which returns blood to the left atrium of the heart.
e: The capillaries carrying oxygenated blood from the alveoli join up to form the pulmonary vein, which returns blood to the left atrium of the heart. The pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood from lungs to the heart. Capillaries are thin-walled vessels where exchange with tissues happens.

q: In fish, the oxygenated blood is distributed to the respiring tissues all over the body directly from the ____.
e: In fish, the oxygenated blood is distributed to the respiring tissues all over the body directly from the gills. Gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces.

q: In insects, the tracheoles which are the finest branches extend close to the surface of nearly every ____.
e: In insects, the tracheoles which are the finest branches extend close to the surface of nearly every cell. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function. Insect tracheoles take air almost to the tissues, so blood need not carry the gases.

q: Homeostasis is the ability of an organism to maintain a relatively constant internal environment, even when the external environment is ____.
e: Homeostasis is the ability of an organism to maintain a relatively constant internal environment, even when the external environment is changing. Homeostasis is keeping the internal environment within narrow limits. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: Successful homeostasis is vital to the survival of any living ____.
e: Successful homeostasis is vital to the survival of any living thing. Homeostasis is keeping the internal environment within narrow limits.

q: Among several organs of plants, leaves may mainly perform for maintaining homeostasis because of their expanded structure and having tiny holes called ____ commonly found on the lower surface.
e: Among several organs of plants, leaves may mainly perform for maintaining homeostasis because of their expanded structure and having tiny holes called stomata commonly found on the lower surface. Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out. Homeostasis is keeping the internal environment within narrow limits.

q: Osmoregulation is the active regulation of osmotic pressure to maintain the balance of water and ____ in an organism.
e: Osmoregulation is the active regulation of osmotic pressure to maintain the balance of water and electrolytes in an organism. Osmoregulation controls water and solute balance.

q: In plant extra water is removed by transpiration and ____.
e: In plant extra water is removed by transpiration and guttation. Guttation pushes liquid water out of hydathodes when root pressure is high. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata.

q: Transpiration is the loss of water from plant ____.
e: Transpiration is the loss of water from plant surface. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata.

q: Of the total water lost from a plant, about 85-90% of water is lost by the ____ transpiration.
e: Of the total water lost from a plant, about 85-90% of water is lost by the stomatal transpiration. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata.

q: Guttation is the expelling of excess water or nutrients through tiny openings (____) on the tips or edges of leaves of some vascular plants.
e: Guttation is the expelling of excess water or nutrients through tiny openings (hydathodes) on the tips or edges of leaves of some vascular plants. Guttation pushes liquid water out of hydathodes when root pressure is high. A vascular system of xylem and phloem is missing in bryophytes.

q: Some plants exude tannins, acids, resins, mucilage, latex, alkaloid, oils and ____ as waste products.
e: Some plants exude tannins, acids, resins, mucilage, latex, alkaloid, oils and gum as waste products. Gum is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Plants also store wastes within their leaves or ____. These wastes are periodically removed as the leaves and barks fall off.
e: Plants also store wastes within their leaves or barks. These wastes are periodically removed as the leaves and barks fall off.

q: Many plants can thermoregulate to maintain relatively stable tissue temperatures in the face of variable environmental ____.
e: Many plants can thermoregulate to maintain relatively stable tissue temperatures in the face of variable environmental temperatures. Temperatures is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Plants use transpiration process to thermoregulate and avoid unfavorable temperature ____.
e: Plants use transpiration process to thermoregulate and avoid unfavorable temperature extremes. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata.

q: Some plants create metabolic heat to actively thermoregulate and attract pollinators or increase growth ____.
e: Some plants create metabolic heat to actively thermoregulate and attract pollinators or increase growth rates. Rates is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Padonmar kya (Nelumbo nucifera) has ____ activities.
e: Padonmar kya (Nelumbo nucifera) has thermoregulation activities. Thermoregulation is the biological term this statement needs.

q: In humans and other mammals, the core body temperature is monitored by a part of the brain called the ____.
e: In humans and other mammals, the core body temperature is monitored by a part of the brain called the thermoregulatory centre. Thermoregulatory centre is the biological term this statement needs.

q: This is located in the ____ of the brain.
e: This is located in the hypothalamus of the brain. The hypothalamus is the brain centre that coordinates thermoregulation and much of homeostasis.

q: Temperature receptors in the skin send electrical impulses to the ____, which stimulates the brain to alter the behaviour.
e: Temperature receptors in the skin send electrical impulses to the hypothalamus, which stimulates the brain to alter the behaviour. The hypothalamus is the brain centre that coordinates thermoregulation and much of homeostasis. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills.

q: Sweating: The sweat glands secrete greater amounts of sweat onto the surface of the skin. When sweat evaporates, it provides a ____ effect.
e: Sweating: The sweat glands secrete greater amounts of sweat onto the surface of the skin. When sweat evaporates, it provides a cooling effect. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills.

q: Vasodilation: The arterioles (small arteries) leading to the capillary loops in the dermis dilate (widen). More blood can flow through these loops, radiating heat to the outside, and cooling the body ____.
e: Vasodilation: The arterioles (small arteries) leading to the capillary loops in the dermis dilate (widen). More blood can flow through these loops, radiating heat to the outside, and cooling the body down. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome. Vasodilation widens skin arterioles so more heat can be lost.

q: Relaxation of hair erector muscles: Hairs on the surface of the skin lie flat on the skin's surface due to the relaxation of the hair erector muscles attached to the base of each hair. This forms the thin layer of trapped air which causes more heat to be ____.
e: Relaxation of hair erector muscles: Hairs on the surface of the skin lie flat on the skin's surface due to the relaxation of the hair erector muscles attached to the base of each hair. This forms the thin layer of trapped air which causes more heat to be lost. Erector pili muscles lift hairs to trap an insulating layer of air. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills.

q: Vasoconstriction: The arterioles (small arteries) leading to the capillary loops in the dermis constrict (narrow). The blood flow to the surface of the skin is reduced, so that less heat is ____.
e: Vasoconstriction: The arterioles (small arteries) leading to the capillary loops in the dermis constrict (narrow). The blood flow to the surface of the skin is reduced, so that less heat is lost. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills.

q: Contraction of hair erector muscles: The hairs are pulled upright by the contraction of hair erector muscles. The hairs trap a layer of air next to the skin which acts as ____.
e: Contraction of hair erector muscles: The hairs are pulled upright by the contraction of hair erector muscles. The hairs trap a layer of air next to the skin which acts as insulation. Erector pili muscles lift hairs to trap an insulating layer of air. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills.

q: Generating more heat: Speeding up of body's metabolism generates more heat. Shivering also takes place due to rapid contraction and relaxation of ____.
e: Generating more heat: Speeding up of body's metabolism generates more heat. Shivering also takes place due to rapid contraction and relaxation of muscles. Shivering makes muscles release heat when the body is too cold.

q: The liver regulates the level of glucose in the ____.
e: The liver regulates the level of glucose in the blood. Blood carries gases, nutrients, hormones, and wastes around the body. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range.

q: The liver stores excess glucose as ____, if the concentration of glucose in the blood gets too high.
e: The liver stores excess glucose as glycogen, if the concentration of glucose in the blood gets too high. Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range.

q: The liver turns glycogen back into glucose if the concentration in the blood gets too ____.
e: The liver turns glycogen back into glucose if the concentration in the blood gets too low. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range. Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals.

q: The brain cells are very sensitive to the glucose concentration in the ____. If the level drops too far, they stop working properly.
e: The brain cells are very sensitive to the glucose concentration in the blood. If the level drops too far, they stop working properly. Blood carries gases, nutrients, hormones, and wastes around the body. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range.

q: Adrenaline raises blood glucose concentration in an ____.
e: Adrenaline raises blood glucose concentration in an emergency. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: If the level of sugar in the blood falls, alpha cells of the Islet of Langerhans in the pancreas release a hormone called ____ into the bloodstream.
e: If the level of sugar in the blood falls, alpha cells of the Islet of Langerhans in the pancreas release a hormone called glucagon into the bloodstream. Glucagon raises blood glucose by triggering glycogen breakdown in the liver. The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin and glucagon.

q: Glucagon acts on the cells in the liver and causes them to convert some of their stored glycogen into ____.
e: Glucagon acts on the cells in the liver and causes them to convert some of their stored glycogen into glucose. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals.

q: Insulin has the opposite effect to ____.
e: Insulin has the opposite effect to glucagon. Glucagon raises blood glucose by triggering glycogen breakdown in the liver. Insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar.

q: If the concentration of blood sugar increases (e.g. after a meal rich in carbohydrate), insulin is released from beta cells of the Islet ____.
e: If the concentration of blood sugar increases (e.g. After a meal rich in carbohydrate), insulin is released from beta cells of the Islet Langerhans. The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin and glucagon. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: When the insulin reaches the liver, it stimulates the liver cells to take up glucose from the blood and store it as ____.
e: When the insulin reaches the liver, it stimulates the liver cells to take up glucose from the blood and store it as glycogen. Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range.

q: Insulin increases the uptake of glucose in all cells for use in ____.
e: Insulin increases the uptake of glucose in all cells for use in respiration. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: Insulin promotes the conversion of carbohydrates to ____.
e: Insulin promotes the conversion of carbohydrates to fats. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar.

q: Insulin slows down the conversion of protein to ____.
e: Insulin slows down the conversion of protein to carbohydrate. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: Osmoregulation is the regulation of water content in the ____.
e: Osmoregulation is the regulation of water content in the blood. Blood carries gases, nutrients, hormones, and wastes around the body. Osmoregulation controls water and solute balance.

q: The more the water loses, the greater the increase in concentration of ____.
e: The more the water loses, the greater the increase in concentration of blood. Blood carries gases, nutrients, hormones, and wastes around the body.

q: ____ function as osmoregulatory organs in most animals.
e: Kidneys function as osmoregulatory organs in most animals. Kidneys excrete urea and regulate water and ions.

q: Humans have two kidneys supplied by the blood from the ____.
e: Humans have two kidneys supplied by the blood from the renal artery. The renal artery brings blood to the kidney. Kidneys excrete urea and regulate water and ions.

q: The kidneys filter about 1,500 litres of blood per day and produce, on average, ____ litres of urine.
e: The kidneys filter about 1,500 litres of blood per day and produce, on average, 1.5 litres of urine. Kidneys excrete urea and regulate water and ions. Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons.

q: Each kidney consists of two regions; the outer region, the cortex and the inner region the ____.
e: Each kidney consists of two regions; the outer region, the cortex and the inner region the medulla. The medulla oblongata contains centres that help control breathing rate. The kidney filters blood, balances water and salts, and forms urine.

q: The medulla has bulges called 'pyramids' pointing towards the concave side of the ____.
e: The medulla has bulges called 'pyramids' pointing towards the concave side of the kidney. The kidney filters blood, balances water and salts, and forms urine. The medulla oblongata contains centres that help control breathing rate.

q: The pyramids lead to a funnel-like structure called the ____.
e: The pyramids lead to a funnel-like structure called the pelvis. Pelvis is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The pelvis connects with the ____, carrying the urine to the bladder.
e: The pelvis connects with the ureter, carrying the urine to the bladder. The ureter carries urine from kidney to bladder. The bladder stores urine until it is released.

q: There are about one million ____ in each kidney.
e: There are about one million nephrons in each kidney. The kidney filters blood, balances water and salts, and forms urine.

q: Nephrons are the basic functional unit of the kidney and each consists of a glomerulus, a Bowman's capsule and a long ____.
e: Nephrons are the basic functional unit of the kidney and each consists of a glomerulus, a Bowman's capsule and a long renal tubule. Bowman's capsule collects filtrate from the glomerulus. The kidney filters blood, balances water and salts, and forms urine.

q: A glomerulus is a cluster of capillaries located inside a cup-like structure called ____.
e: A glomerulus is a cluster of capillaries located inside a cup-like structure called Bowman's capsule. Bowman's capsule collects filtrate from the glomerulus. Capillaries are thin-walled vessels where exchange with tissues happens.

q: A renal tubule comprises of three portions: the proximal convoluted tubule, the loop of Henle and the ____.
e: A renal tubule comprises of three portions: the proximal convoluted tubule, the loop of Henle and the distal convoluted tubule. The distal convoluted tubule fine-tunes salts and pH of the forming urine. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: The tubules of all the nephrons join with the ____.
e: The tubules of all the nephrons join with the collecting duct. The collecting duct makes final water adjustments under ADH.

q: The nephron carries out its function in four steps: ultrafiltration, secretion, selective reabsorption and ____.
e: The nephron carries out its function in four steps: ultrafiltration, secretion, selective reabsorption and excretion. Nephrons are the kidney's filtering and urine-forming units. Four major environment components together are called the ecosphere.

q: Ultrafiltration is the process, where the filter separates different sized molecules under ____.
e: Ultrafiltration is the process, where the filter separates different sized molecules under pressure. Pressure is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The pressure of the blood in the arteriole leading to the glomerulus is very ____. This pressure forces fluid from the blood through the walls of the capillaries and the Bowman's capsule.
e: The pressure of the blood in the arteriole leading to the glomerulus is very high. This pressure forces fluid from the blood through the walls of the capillaries and the Bowman's capsule. Bowman's capsule collects filtrate from the glomerulus. Capillaries are thin-walled vessels where exchange with tissues happens.

q: The fluid that diffuses out of the glomerulus is called ____ which contains glucose, salts, vitamins, wastes such as urea and other small molecules.
e: The fluid that diffuses out of the glomerulus is called filtrate which contains glucose, salts, vitamins, wastes such as urea and other small molecules. Glomerular filtrate is the fluid forced into Bowman's capsule. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: Secretion is the active and selective uptake of molecules that did not get filtered into ____.
e: Secretion is the active and selective uptake of molecules that did not get filtered into Bowman's capsule. Bowman's capsule collects filtrate from the glomerulus.

q: Selective reabsorption is the process by which most of water and solutes (glucose, amino acids and some salts that are needed by the body) that initially entered the renal tubule during filtration are selectively reabsorbed and transported back into the ____ that surround the tubule.
e: Selective reabsorption is the process by which most of water and solutes (glucose, amino acids and some salts that are needed by the body) that initially entered the renal tubule during filtration are selectively reabsorbed and transported back into the capillaries that surround the tubule. Capillaries are thin-walled vessels where exchange with tissues happens. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon.

q: This process occurs in the proximal convoluted tubule, the loop of Henle, the distal convoluted tubule and the ____.
e: This process occurs in the proximal convoluted tubule, the loop of Henle, the distal convoluted tubule and the collecting duct. The collecting duct makes final water adjustments under ADH. The distal convoluted tubule fine-tunes salts and pH of the forming urine.

q: The longer the loop of Henle, the greater the reabsorption of ____.
e: The longer the loop of Henle, the greater the reabsorption of water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis.

q: Excretion is the removal of metabolic wastes, such as ____ wastes.
e: Excretion is the removal of metabolic wastes, such as nitrogenous wastes. Nitrogenous is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Everything that passes into the collecting duct is now called ____.
e: Everything that passes into the collecting duct is now called urine. Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons. The collecting duct makes final water adjustments under ADH.

q: The ureter carries the urine from the pelvis to the ____, in which the urine is temporarily stored.
e: The ureter carries the urine from the pelvis to the bladder, in which the urine is temporarily stored. The bladder stores urine until it is released. The ureter carries urine from kidney to bladder.

q: Urine is then periodically excreted from the body through ____.
e: Urine is then periodically excreted from the body through urethra. The urethra is the tube that releases urine from the bladder. Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons.

q: Homeostasis is typically achieved via negative feedback loops, but can be affected by ____ feedback loops.
e: Homeostasis is typically achieved via negative feedback loops, but can be affected by positive feedback loops. Homeostasis is keeping the internal environment within narrow limits.

q: Negative feedback is a control system, in which receptor detects changes in the internal environment away from the normal and acts to return the internal environment back to a steady ____.
e: Negative feedback is a control system, in which receptor detects changes in the internal environment away from the normal and acts to return the internal environment back to a steady state. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: One of the negative feedback loops in plants is their responses to water ____.
e: One of the negative feedback loops in plants is their responses to water limitations. Limitations is the biological term this statement needs.

q: 'Diuresis' means the flow of urine from the body, so 'antidiuresis' means producing ____ urine.
e: 'Diuresis' means the flow of urine from the body, so 'antidiuresis' means producing less urine. Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons.

q: The Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) starts to work when the body loses too much water, for example if sweating heavily and not replacing lost water by ____.
e: The Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) starts to work when the body loses too much water, for example if sweating heavily and not replacing lost water by drinking. ADH, antidiuretic hormone, makes the kidney reabsorb more water.

q: When the concentration of the blood starts to increase, the receptor cells in the ____ of the brain detects.
e: When the concentration of the blood starts to increase, the receptor cells in the hypothalamus of the brain detects. The hypothalamus is the brain centre that coordinates thermoregulation and much of homeostasis.

q: These cells are sensitive to the solute concentration of the blood, and stimulate the pituitary gland to release more ____.
e: These cells are sensitive to the solute concentration of the blood, and stimulate the pituitary gland to release more ADH. ADH, antidiuretic hormone, makes the kidney reabsorb more water.

q: At the kidneys, ADH causes the collecting ducts to become more permeable to ____, so that more water is reabsorbed back into the blood.
e: At the kidneys, ADH causes the collecting ducts to become more permeable to water, so that more water is reabsorbed back into the blood. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Kidneys excrete urea and regulate water and ions.

q: When the blood is too dilute, the opposite happens and the pituitary produces less ____. This in turn stimulates the collecting duct to absorb less water.
e: When the blood is too dilute, the opposite happens and the pituitary produces less ADH. This in turn stimulates the collecting duct to absorb less water. ADH, antidiuretic hormone, makes the kidney reabsorb more water. The collecting duct makes final water adjustments under ADH.

q: Positive feedback is a mechanism which amplifies or speeds up a physiological response, usually to achieve a particular ____.
e: Positive feedback is a mechanism which amplifies or speeds up a physiological response, usually to achieve a particular outcome. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water.

q: A positive feedback mechanism stops when the ____ result is achieved.
e: A positive feedback mechanism stops when the end result is achieved. End is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Positive feedback in plants: Fruit ripening is one of the examples of a positive biological feedback loop in ____.
e: Positive feedback in plants: Fruit ripening is one of the examples of a positive biological feedback loop in plants. Plants is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Fruits in a pile of mature mangoes ripen one after another very quickly. This will begin with the first mango to ripen. Once ripe, it gives off a gas called ____ through its skin.
e: Fruits in a pile of mature mangoes ripen one after another very quickly. This will begin with the first mango to ripen. Once ripe, it gives off a gas called ethylene through its skin. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills.

q: When exposed to this gas, the mangoes near to it also ____. Once ripe, they too produce ethylene gas.
e: When exposed to this gas, the mangoes near to it also ripen. Once ripe, they too produce ethylene gas.

q: Positive feedback in animals: A baby suckling on the mother's nipple will activate receptors in the ____.
e: Positive feedback in animals: A baby suckling on the mother's nipple will activate receptors in the nipple. Nipple is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The receptors will send signals to the brain via neurons telling the pituitary gland to release two important hormones; prolactin and ____.
e: The receptors will send signals to the brain via neurons telling the pituitary gland to release two important hormones; prolactin and oxytocin. Oxytocin is a hypothalamic hormone involved in birth and milk ejection. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Prolactin stimulates milk production in the breast ____, while oxytocin stimulates smooth muscles contraction of the breast allowing the milk to eject out of the nipples.
e: Prolactin stimulates milk production in the breast tissues, while oxytocin stimulates smooth muscles contraction of the breast allowing the milk to eject out of the nipples. Oxytocin is a hypothalamic hormone involved in birth and milk ejection.

q: The more the baby sucks, the greater the amount of milk ____.
e: The more the baby sucks, the greater the amount of milk produces. Produces is the biological term this statement needs.
